The strongest direct evidence concerns duplicate products, rather than TF-IDF specifically. [Basaran, Ntoutsi and Zimek (SDM 2017)](https://www.kbs.uni-hannover.de/~ntoutsi/papers/17.SDM.pdf) show that Amazon item-variant redundancies distort recommendation evaluation, with effects differing by algorithm complexity. This supports auditing duplicate groups, but does not establish description boilerplate as the mechanism. [TASTE (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.14029) reports text-based sequential recommendation gains associated with reduced popularity bias; its language-model results do not validate TF-IDF lexical recurrence. I found no directly matching study jointly isolating duplicate descriptions, brand boilerplate, metadata missingness and residual magnitude with all the requested controls.

For temporal controls, [Petrov et al. (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19833) find that simple recency-weighted pairwise models outperform Transformer reproductions on several Amazon benchmarks. These results motivate last-item, recency-weighted co-occurrence and popularity baselines before attributing gains to richer temporal understanding. They concern different datasets/protocols and cannot establish the outcome for the four specified categories.

Recommended diagnostics—not a published, validated control suite: permute whole item texts within category, training-popularity, text-length and missingness strata, preserving empty fields; compare raw text against repeated-template removal and title-only/description-only variants. Keep benchmark splits/candidates fixed and report validation slices excluding cases where target and history share exact/near-duplicate text groups. Compare against recency-only and popularity-only scoring. For additive text corrections, compare the true correction with candidate-permuted corrections preserving each user’s correction magnitudes, plus scale-matched random corrections. Report paired HR@10 changes, uncertainty, nonzero lexical-match coverage, and gains by popularity/missingness stratum. Sparse coverage or surviving permutation gains would weaken a semantic or temporal interpretation.
